To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the upset threshold of a static RAM is 2.2 MeV cm2 mg-1, that the upset cross-section of a 4K-bit GaAs RAM is 1.5 x 10-6 cm2 and that the upset cross section of a 16K-bit GaAs static RAM is 1 x 10-7 cm2.
The first measurement of SEU cross-sections for GaAs SRAMs caused by heavy ion bombardment was performed.
the SEU cross sections of the circuits are very low and that the LET threshold of the circuits is about 1.5 x 105 keV/micrometers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effect of ionizing particles on the electrical characteristics of semiconductor devices.
the development of a high-speed, low-power, and low-cost GaAs static RAM (SRAM) for space applications, and the investigation of the radiation effects of heavy ions on GaAs SRAMs.
the development of GaAs MESFET's for high-speed and low-noise applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GaAs RAMs are not immune to heavy ion upset.
the SEU threshold LET of GaAs static RAM is 1.5 times higher than that of silicon static RAMs, and GaAs static RAM has a lower cross-section than silicon static RAM.
GaAs RAMs are not more sensitive to single event upsets than silicon RAMs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GaAs RAMs are much more sensitive to heavy ions than their silicon counterparts.
the GaAs RAMs are more susceptible to heavy ion induced upset than the Si RAMs.
the SEU sensitivity of GaAs static RAM is comparable to that of Si static RAMs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GaAs static RAM is a very sensitive memory element.
GaAs static RAM cells are much more susceptible to SEU than their Si counterparts.
the SEU cross-section for GaAs SRAMs is comparable to the cross-section of silicon SRAMs for the same LET.
